Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-03

Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE), Luca Moretti (Redwood), Priya Rao (Redwood Product), Ethan Wu (Polaris), Sofia Alvarez (Polaris), Dr. Lila Sharma (Polaris), Omar Rizvi (Polaris SRE)

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Maya, AE for Redwood, and Jordan our SE will run the lab. Today we'll show how to pick a quant profile for production, mostly INT8 vs FP8, and the Console observability you'll use to detect fidelity regressions.
[00:02:00] Jordan: Hi, thanks. I want to start with the high-level tradeoff: FP8 tends to give better fidelity at the cost of higher memory/compute, INT8 gives the biggest cost savings but you need to validate per-prompt quality. We'll walk examples.
[00:04:00] Ethan: Quick context from our side — we're running a clinical summarization pipeline, 1k reqs/day now, target 50k in 6 months. Latency SLO is 350ms p95. Cost is a big driver but we can't accept hallucination increases.
[00:06:00] Sofia: Also we want VPC peering and customer-managed KMS, and some of our data must stay in region. We ran a small in-house INT8 test and saw weird tokenization artifacts, so curious how Redwood handles that.
[00:08:00] Jordan: Good callouts. On VPC/KMS that's supported in Private mode; for hosted we offer VPC peering options and KMS integration — Luca can share details after. Regarding tokenization artifacts, often INT8 sensitivity is prompt-dependent; Optimize helps you pick a profile per route so lower-risk routes can use INT8 while high-risk routes stay on FP8.
[00:10:00] Priya: I want to show the Console screen where we surface per-prompt quality diffs. You can set a fidelity threshold — say we tolerate up to 0.5% drop in QA accuracy — and Console flags violations and can auto-roll back to a safer profile.
[00:12:00] Jordan: I'll pull up the live Console. (click) Ok you can see here baseline metrics: token latency distribution, cost per 1k tokens, and a fidelity heatmap derived from eval set. Note: our auto-eval uses a mix of ROUGE/QA exact match and fuzzy embedding similarity — it's configurable.
[00:14:00] Dr. Lila: Quick question: how is 'fidelity' computed? We need something clinically defensible, not just BLEU.
[00:16:00] Jordan: Right — for clinical use cases we recommend combined metrics: domain-specific QA exact match for critical facts, plus embedding-similarity for phrasing. You can plug your own eval harness; we ingest results and show deltas per-deploy.
[00:18:00] Ethan: About benchmarking — what's your suggested bench for INT8/FP8? We want to run it on our sample prompts and see real latency numbers.
[00:20:00] Jordan: Our bench template (shared) runs three modes: single-request p95 latency sweep, concurrency sweep up to expected QPS, and fidelity sweep where we compare outputs to your golden set. Important to run with KV cache warm for summarization workloads to reflect production.
[00:22:00] Sofia: You mentioned warm cache — we mostly do single prompts, but we do use context windows ~1k tokens. How does that change the INT8 penalty?
[00:24:00] Jordan: Longer contexts amplify memory bandwidth differences; FP8 often wins for long-context quality because quantization error compounds, but INT8 still usually gives latency wins. The Console's profile recommendations take historical seq length distribution into account.
[00:26:00] Maya: Let's show a quick AB: here's our test transcript. Baseline (fp8-safest) yields p95 420ms and QA exact-match 94.2%. INT8-fast yields p95 290ms but QA drops to 92.1% on this set. That's a 2.1 point drop — maybe unacceptable for clinical facts.
[00:28:00] Dr. Lila: 2 points seems risky. Which types of errors are these — hallucination or omission?
[00:30:00] Jordan: Mostly omission on secondary details and slight paraphrase changes. We can break down by token-level alignments in Console. Often a hybrid approach works: keep FP8 for routes that extract key facts and use INT8 for bulk paraphrase/summary where tolerance is higher.
[00:32:00] Ethan: Could we do a per-route policy? For e.g., 'discharge-summary' route is FP8, 'patient-education' route INT8?
[00:34:00] Jordan: Absolutely — you can pin profiles per route or do automatic routing by policy (latency-first vs fidelity-first). We also support dynamic fallback: try INT8, if fidelity delta > threshold then fallback to FP8 in real-time.
[00:36:00] Sofia: What about cost math? Show me ballpark savings.
[00:38:00] Maya: On our pricing model, switching route to INT8 can reduce per-token compute costs by ~35-50% depending on hardware. For your 50k/day projection, that could be tens of thousands per month, but exact depends on batching. We'll include a modeled spreadsheet.
[00:40:00] Luca: On hardware, Gpu generations matter — INT8 kernels are very efficient on A100/A200 series; on older hardware the gains shrink. If you go Dedicated, we can match model variant to node type for best raw latency.
[00:42:00] Omar: Network jitter is our concern — pe95 spikes come from backend. If we see occasional network blips, do fallbacks add instability?
[00:44:00] Jordan: The runtime is built for graceful degradation. If a profile hits resource contention, Smart Routing can shift requests to a higher-capacity variant or region. Console shows traces so you can correlate fidelity drops to infra events.
[00:46:00] Priya: A quick note on rollout patterns: we recommend canary 5–10% with close eval hooks, then 25% if metrics hold, then full. Console can enforce automatic rollback if fidelity breaches, and you can set a cooldown period.
[00:48:00] Maya: Let's capture the concrete pilot: we'll run a 2-week bench on your prompts. Jordan will run INT8/FP8 sweeps and provide raw traces; we'll give a cost projection and recommended per-route profile mapping.
[00:50:00] Ethan: Sounds good. One last ops question: how long to switch a profile in production? Is it a model deploy or config flip?
[00:51:00] Jordan: It's a config flip — the model binary stays the same, we switch runtime quantized kernels or profile parameters. Typically sub-second per-instance, but global rollout depends on your routing policy.
[00:51:30] Maya: Great—thanks everyone. We'll share the benchmark template and pricing. Follow-up scheduled after we get your prompt set.
[00:52:00] End of transcript.
